answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by tying voting weight to a locked bond instead of to a cheap identity. Every newcomer posts a jade deposit that is slashed the instant it is caught signing twice. Minting fake agents is nearly free; funding them is not. To control k votes an attacker must lock k separate deposits, so the cost rises linearly with the clone count. A prism cross-check of overlapping signers reveals reused keys, and one duplicate burns the whole ember of collateral, leaving the foe nothing to recycle.
